newsitem.title: UK: London gold makes litle headway, others firmer.
newsitem.headline: London gold makes litle headway, others firmer.

text.p: Gold managed only a 35-cent rise between its fixes on Thursday after latest U.S. economic data showed few tensions in the economy.
But while gold was struggling, the other precious metals firmed from earlier levels and although highs were not sustained, they remained above last night's close.
Gold was fixed at $326.35 per ounce up from $326.00 this morning but under Wednesday's $327.55. The December contract on Comex was just $0.20 ahead at $330.80.
There was little momentum behind the market after latest U.S. economic data showed weekly jobless insurance claims fell to their lowest since 1974 in the week ended July 26.
The U.S. second quarter GDP price deflator rose only 1.4 pct, the smallest gain since the second quarter 1964.
"Gold has tried a few times to get above $330.00 recently but there just isn't the will. Unless something happens outside of the market we are in a $325-$330 range," a dealer said.
It was a different story for silver which was indicated at $4.45/$4.47 up eight cents having made a more sustained effort than recently to establish itself over $4.40.
Dealers and technical analysts had been saying all week that silver's technial background looked more psotive than gold but critical mass of buying was not achieved until today.
The push came from the Comex locals who triggered stops and firmed the September contract to $4.49 before it came back to $4.45 up 7.2 cents after the bullion fixing.
"There is definitely more potential in silver than gold medium term," one dealer said.

The platinum group metals were also firmer but off their highs. Platinum fixed at its highest point since June 12 at $435.00 and palladium equalled its morning fix of $211.00. Deales said some PGM parcels were being bought by European dealers loco Zurich from Russia's Almaz export agency but the market remained extremely tight.
Fund buying of palladium especially has moved prices higher this week.
Palladium has also firmed on short covering by speculators on Tocom who faced margin calls as the price rose putting the market limit up on Wednesay.
Dealers quoted one month lease rates at 25 percent for platinum and 75 percent for palladium.
